waveName: Wave 4 – Cut placement & accents, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detection

package.title: Laying workbench: section focus, brush/rectangle marking, next stone, undo taps, material view switch
package.goal: At the work table, the user can focus on one section and see live open counts per colour. They can mark stones by tap, brush or rectangle, undo mistakes, and step through 'next stone' cards that show the cut instructions. The material and shopping view gets its own full-width tab.
steps: Move MaterialCalc out of StepPlan into MaterialCalc.tsx without changing its behaviour. Add a top-level Segmented control 'Verlegen | Material & Einkauf' above the viewer layout. The material view renders full width without the viewer.

Section focus: in laying mode with a section selected, pass focusRange={sec} to the Viewer. A tap outside shows 'Stein gehört zu Abschnitt X – wechseln?'.
Colour chips from progressByColor for the section or the whole project, e.g. '06 · 37/112 offen'. Tapping a chip sets focusColor.
SectionLegend takes laid counts from progressByColor, not from the worker stats.

Marking modes Tippen | Malen | Rechteck:
- Malen: onPaint sets bits per piece.
- Rechteck: confirm 'N Steine als verlegt markieren?', then setRangePlaced.
- After each gesture call api.touchProgress(dirtyCells).
- Undo stack of 50 entries: piece toggles, plus progress slices for ranges. 'Rückgängig (n)' button.
- Status line, e.g. 'AP034 als verlegt markiert', plus the flash highlight.
- 'Abschnitt fertig' asks for confirmation when the section is partly laid.

Next-stone card, sticky at the bottom on phones:
- Content: ID, colour code and swatch, size, and the cut text from the exported cutInstruction. Export it from StoneDialog with no other change there. If a piece does not fit, show cut.notFit.
- Buttons: '✓ verlegt & weiter', 'zurück', 'überspringen', 'Reihe fertig' (row order only), 'Details' (opens StoneDialog).
- Order toggle Reihe/Farbe. Remember the section and order in localStorage inside try/catch.
- Screen wake lock, feature-detected and re-requested on visibilitychange.
Add a 'PDF {sec}' shortcut: set rec.pdfOptions.sectionIds = [sec.id] through api.update and navigate the hash to /pdf. Wrap the CSV export in await + catch with a visible error message.
acceptance: Unit tests: for the 4 samples, progressByColor totals per section sum to progressOf. layingOrder visits every piece of the range exactly once. Undo restores exact counts, including partly laid sections.

e2e: select B2, turn on laying mode, tap inside A1: placed-count is unchanged. Three times '✓ verlegt & weiter' then Rückgängig: placed-count is 2. A rectangle drag adds exactly that range's pieces. Finding 'ZZ9999' shows the not-found message. The Material tab has no horizontal page overflow at 1440 px.
package.risk: Effort L. The undo stack lives only for the session; say so in the UI. Make sure the paint and rectangle modes never fire from normal scrolling on phones.

findings.title: Laying mode has no row/column orientation and no bulk marking; progress is only per tap or whole section
findings.problem: While laying, the user has to find 'row AI, column 34' on the screen, but the viewer draws only section labels and colour codes, with no row letters, column numbers or ruler. In Verlegemodus, dragging pans instead of marking, so a 40×50 cm portrait (5,969 stones) needs thousands of taps unless a whole 30×30 cm section is marked at once. 'Meine Projekte' does not show laying progress.

findings.proposal: 1) In Viewer.tsx, add sticky top/left gutter overlays (spreadsheet-style) that print column numbers and row letters from layout.colX/rowY for the visible range, shown once stones are at least about 12 px. Add a matching 'Gehe zu' field in the plan step. 2) Lay mode: pointer-drag paints 'verlegt' on every touched piece (Space or two fingers to pan); Shift-drag a rectangle uses the existing setRangePlaced(). Add 'Reihe bis hier verlegt' and 'nächster offener Stein' buttons. 3) Make laid stones clearly visible (desaturated plus check mark). 4) Show '% verlegt' and a mini progress bar per project in Projects.tsx and the home recent cards; progressOf() already exists.
corrected:
1) Row and column labels on screen. In Viewer.tsx, add a thin top and left gutter (about 18 px), drawn in renderMosaic after the cells or as a separate overlay canvas. Use visibleRange(layout, view) to get the visible rows and columns. Print rowLabel(row) at rowY[row]+rowH[row]/2 and col+1 at colX[col]+colW[col]/2, with the same label-skipping rule the PDF uses (labelStep in pdf.ts:605, applied to pitchPx): every label when pitch is at least 14 px, every 5th or 10th when smaller, none in overview mode. This keeps the screen and PDF labels identical. Also highlight the row and column of the selected stone in the gutter.

2) 'Find stone' in the plan step. Move the parseCellId form from StepPreview.tsx:62-77 into a shared component and use it in StepPlan as well. It should centre the stone and highlight it, and in laying mode it should not toggle it.

3) Bulk marking as an explicit choice. Add a Segmented control next to the 'Verlegemodus' toggle with three options: Tippen (current behaviour), Pinsel (paint) and Rechteck (rectangle).
- Pinsel: a one-pointer drag sets laid=true on every piece it touches, or laid=false if the first piece touched was already laid. Use setCellPlaced or a per-piece set, not a toggle, so going over a stone twice does not undo it.
- Rechteck: a drag draws a rectangle, then calls setRangePlaced(layout, data, {r0,r1,c0,c1}, true) for the cells it covers.
- In both modes, two fingers (touch) or Space / middle button (desktop) pan the view, and the cursor changes to crosshair.
- Keep one step of undo: snapshot data.progress before each stroke and show an 'Rückgängig' button.
- In StoneDialog, add 'Reihe in diesem Abschnitt verlegt' and 'Spalte in diesem Abschnitt verlegt'. Use setRangePlaced with {r0:row,r1:row+1,c0:sec.c0,c1:sec.c1} (and the matching column range).
- Add a 'Nächster offener Stein' button: scan data.progress from the start of the selected section, then centre and highlight the first piece that is not laid.

4) Progress in Meine Projekte and on Home. Do not call progressOf() in the list. In useProject.touchProgress and the compute save, write meta.progressPlaced and meta.progressTotal from the progress memo that already exists (useProject.ts:224) and save the record with saveProject. Projects.tsx and the Home cards then show 'NN % verlegt' and a small ProgressBar from these two numbers. If the fields are missing (older projects), show nothing until the project is next opened.

Leave out the original sub-proposal on making laid stones visible: drawPlaced in render.ts already does this. At most, make the check mark appear from 6 px instead of 10 px.

1) Rulers on screen (S-M). Add a 'rulers' option to RenderOptions in src/core/render.ts and turn it on in StepPlan/StepPreview.
- Draw a top band and a left band of about 18 px.
- Put column numbers (col+1) at layout.colX[col]+colW/2 and row labels from rowLabel(row) at rowY+rowH/2, only for the visibleRange.
- When the pitch is under about 14 px, label only every 5th or 10th index so labels do not overlap.
- Use exactly the same labels as cellId() and pdf.ts:617.
- On desktop, add a small status line under the viewer: the hovered stone's pieceId plus X/Y in mm from the existing origin. Compute it with the same indexAt and pointInPolygon logic as onUp.
- Move the existing 'find stone' field (parseCellId, StepPreview.tsx:66-73) into a shared component. Use it in StepPlan too, so it centres and highlights the stone.

2) Faster marking (M). Under the Verlegemodus toggle, add a mode switch: Tippen | Malen | Rechteck.
- In Malen, one-finger or mouse drag sets every piece it touches to the state opposite to the first touched piece. Two fingers (or Space/middle mouse) pan and zoom.
- In Rechteck, drag a cell-snapped rectangle, show 'N Steine als verlegt markieren?', then call setRangePlaced().
- Snapshot data.progress (a Uint16Array copy) before each gesture and add a 'Rückgängig' button with a short history of 10-20 steps.
- During a gesture, call only draw(). Call api.touchProgress() once on pointerup so progressOf over all sections does not run on every move.
- Add 'Nächster offener Stein': in the selected section, or globally, row-major, find the first piece whose progress bit is 0, then centre and highlight it with its ID.
- Drop 'Reihe bis hier verlegt' for now because what it should do is unclear.

3) Visibility of laid stones (S). Keep the existing tick (it already works). Replace the white wash with a desaturating grey or green tint, which also shows on white or light stones. In the overview path (pitch under 3 px), draw a second 1-pixel-per-cell progress overlay so progress is visible on large projects when the whole mosaic is shown.

4) Progress in the project list (S). Do not load mosaics in Projects.tsx. Add an optional field to ProjectMeta: progressSummary {placed, total}.
- Update it wherever progress is saved (the touchProgress save callback and the save after compute in useProject.ts) using progressOf(), and save it with the project.
- Clear it on recompute.
- In Projects.tsx and the Home recent cards, show 'x % verlegt' with a mini ProgressBar only when the field exists. Otherwise show nothing rather than an estimate.

findings.title: No guided laying or section workbench: laying mode only toggles single taps on the full mosaic
findings.problem: Requirements 10 and 14 (edit sections separately; laid, open and remaining stones) are met only minimally. Laying mode toggles the tapped piece and nothing else. The Plan viewer has no colour filter, although Viewer and render support focusColor. Selecting a section only zooms; the rest of the mosaic stays visible and tappable. There is no laying order, no 'next stone', no 'whole row laid' and no phone-friendly card. These are what a person at the workbench actually needs.
findings.evidence: src/ui/project/StepPlan.tsx:98-101: layMode → togglePiecePlaced on the tapped piece only. focusColor is passed only in src/ui/project/StepPreview.tsx:53, not in StepPlan. Section click → viewer.current?.zoomTo(x) (StepPlan.tsx:158), with no clipping. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/shots/b1-plan.png.
findings.proposal: Add a 'Verlegen' workbench in StepPlan. 1) Choose a section; render only its Range (r0..r1, c0..c1) and grey out the rest. Restrict taps and edits to that range. 2) Colour chips from the existing per-section stats (sectionStats or SectionLegend), with counters such as '06: 37 von 112 offen in B2'. Pass focusColor to the Viewer. 3) A 'Nächster Stein' button computes the next unplaced piece in a chosen order: by colour, then serpentine by row. This uses only existing data, with no new geometry. Show a large card with ID, code, size and cut instruction (cutInstruction). Buttons: 'verlegt ✓ & weiter', 'zurück', 'ganze Reihe verlegt'. 4) Keep the screen on with navigator.wakeLock where supported. 5) Add 'Abschnitt drucken', which calls the existing PDF worker with sectionIds:[id], and 'CSV Abschnitt'.
corrected:
Add a 'Verlegen' workbench in StepPlan.tsx. It uses only existing data, with no new geometry. Order of value:

1) Section focus (S-M):
- Add `focusRange?: Range | null` to RenderOptions in render.ts and to ViewerProps.
- After the cell and overview pass, paint a semi-opaque overlay over the four rectangles outside the range. Base them on the section's x/y/w/h ± joint/2. This also covers the overview path (pitchPx<3).
- In Viewer onUp, drop picks where row/col fall outside the range.
- In StepPlan, pass focusRange={layMode && sec ? sec : null}. Add a 'Nur Abschnitt' toggle so the user can still see the whole picture.

2) Colour filter in Plan (S):
- Render clickable chips from api.sectionStats.get(sec.id).perColor, or from api.stats when no section is selected. This data already holds pieces and placed per colour.
- Label them like '06 · 37/112 offen'. Pass focusColor to the Viewer.
- Change render.ts so out-of-focus pieces use a grey dim (e.g. rgba(128,128,128,0.7)) instead of the same white wash used for 'placed'. Otherwise laid pieces cannot be told apart under the filter.

3) Row actions (S):
- In laying mode, a long-press on a stone, or a 'Reihe verlegt' button for the currently picked row, calls setRangePlaced(layout, data, {r0:row, r1:row+1, c0:sec.c0, c1:sec.c1}, true). Then call api.touchProgress().
- Ask for confirmation, as the existing reset button does.

4) 'Nächster Stein' card (M):
- Add a pure helper in edits.ts: nextUnplaced(layout, data, range, {color?, order:'serpentine'}) → {row, col, piece}|null. It scans the range row by row (alternating direction), checks data.progress bits against cellPieceCount, and optionally filters by piece colour.
- Unit-test it in tests/.
- Show a large bottom card (sticky on mobile) with:
  - the pieceId
  - the colour code and swatch
  - the size
  - the cut lines, taken from a component extracted from StoneDialog's existing analyzeCut-based cut list (do not re-derive the dimensions)
- Card buttons:
  - '✓ verlegt & weiter': togglePiecePlaced, then touchProgress, then nextUnplaced, then viewer.center()
  - 'zurück': keep a small history stack
  - 'Details': opens StoneDialog

5) Optional: keep the screen awake only through feature detection ('wakeLock' in navigator). Plan for a Capacitor keep-awake plugin for the APK, because the Android WebView may not expose the API.

Drop 'CSV Abschnitt'; it already exists at StepPlan.tsx:226. Replace 'Abschnitt drucken' with a link that switches to step 10 with opts.sectionIds=[sec.id] pre-selected (StepPdf.tsx:131-144 already supports it).

Files: src/ui/project/StepPlan.tsx, src/ui/project/Viewer.tsx, src/core/render.ts, src/core/edits.ts (nextUnplaced), src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx (extract the cut list), the i18n de/en/tr files, and tests/.

Build a "Verlegen" workbench in StepPlan, using only existing data.

1) Section focus and protected taps (the biggest win)
- Add `focusRange?: Range` to RenderOptions. In renderMosaic, after drawing the cells, paint `rgba(255,255,255,0.7)` over the four rectangles outside the range. Put the sections overlay on top.
- StepPlan passes `focusRange={sec}` while a section is selected.
- In lay mode, onPick ignores taps outside sec (r < sec.r0 || r >= sec.r1 || c < sec.c0 || c >= sec.c1). Show a short note instead: "Stein gehört zu Abschnitt X – Abschnitt wechseln?".
- Also ignore toggles when the tapped stone is smaller than about 8 px on screen. Instead, zoom in with center(x, y, minScale) so the stone becomes tappable.
- Add an undo stack in StepPlan: up to 100 entries of {idx, prevMask}, set for every progress change, including setRangePlaced on whole rows. Add a "Rückgängig" button. Call api.touchProgress() after each change.

2) Colour filter with live counters
- Add `progressByColor(layout, data, range)` to src/core/stats.ts. It works like progressOf, with no geometry:
  - FULL → c1
  - SUB → data.sub
  - FREE → data.free[i].color
  - DIAG/LINE → c1 or c2 for piece 0 or 1
  - The placed bit is `(progress[idx] >> i) & 1`.
- It returns Map<color, {placed, total}> and is computed in a useMemo on [sec, version, progressVersion].
- Show swatch chips with "06 · 37 / 112 offen". A tap sets `focusColor` on the Viewer; tap again to clear.
- Do not use the debounced worker sectionStats for these counters.
- Test: the totals summed over all colours equal progressOf(range) for every section of all four sample projects.

3) "Nächster Stein" card
- From the section's cells, build an ordered list of (idx, piece) pairs. Two orders, chosen by toggle:
  - "Reihe für Reihe": serpentine row order, pieces in index order
  - "Farbe für Farbe": colours by code, then serpentine row order inside each colour
  - If a colour filter is active, use only that colour.
- Rebuild the list when `version` changes, after mosaic edits. Do not store the cursor: it is always the first unplaced entry, or the next one after the current entry.
- The card content must come from the same helpers as StoneDialog, so the text matches the dialog, PDF and CSV:
  - ID from cellId plus "-n" for split pieces
  - colour code and swatch
  - size from analyzeCut(...).w/h
  - the exported cutInstruction(info, ...)
  - If info.fits is false, show the existing cut.notFit message. Never show an invented cut.
- Highlight the stone with the existing `highlight` prop and center it with viewer.center(x, y, 12).
- Buttons:
  - "verlegt ✓ & weiter"
  - "zurück"
  - "überspringen"
  - "Reihe fertig", only in row order: setRangePlaced on {r0: row, r1: row+1, c0: sec.c0, c1: sec.c1}
  - "Rückgängig"
- On a phone, the card is a sticky bar at the bottom of the screen.
- Save the chosen section and order with the project (settings or kv) so work resumes there.
- Test: the order generator visits every piece in the range exactly once, and its length equals progressOf(range).total.

4) Keep the screen on
- When "Verlegen" is active, request the screen wake lock (`'wakeLock' in navigator` → request('screen')). Re-request it on visibilitychange.
- If it is unsupported, do nothing; there is no error. In the Android WebView it may not be available. If it is not, add the keep-awake Capacitor plugin later.

5) Shortcuts only
- "Abschnitt als PDF" opens step 10 with sectionIds=[sec.id] already set.
- Drop "CSV Abschnitt" from the proposal; it already exists (StepPlan.tsx:226).

E2E check: select B2, turn on lay mode, tap in A1 → placed-count stays the same. Then "verlegt & weiter" three times followed by "Rückgängig" → placed-count = 2.

findings.title: Laying mode and stone taps at overview zoom hit random stones (about 6 px per stone); taps 4 px apart lay three different stones and there is no undo
findings.problem: The plan step opens fitted to the screen. On a phone the 30x40 cm portrait sample is drawn at about 1 CSS px per mm, so one 5 mm stone plus joint is about 6 CSS px, roughly 1 mm on the physical screen. A fingertip covers dozens of stones. In laying mode every tap without movement toggles whatever stone lies under the touch point. A finger offset of 4 px already lays a different stone. At this zoom nothing visible changes, so the user does not notice, and README states there is no undo. The tap slop is 5 px (Viewer.tsx:201), smaller than typical finger jitter, and long presses also count as taps (downAt.t is never used). The preview has the same problem: taps 3 px apart open different stones.

Screenshot .../shots/m-touch.png (right panel): 3 stones marked as laid, with no visible marker at fit zoom. Canvas size 340x523 CSS px for 300x400 mm. Code: StepPlan.tsx:120-126 (togglePiecePlaced on every pick), Viewer.tsx:196-244.
findings.proposal: In Viewer.onUp, for pointerType 'touch' or 'pen', compute the on-screen stone size, min(layout.tileW, layout.tileH) * view.scale. If it is below 24 px, do not call onPick. Instead animate a zoom centred on the tap point to the scale where a stone is about 36 px, and show the hint 'Zum Verlegen hineinzoomen'. Raise the touch tap slop to 10 px and ignore presses longer than 500 ms. After each toggle in laying mode, flash the stone outline for 400 ms and call navigator.vibrate?.(10). In StepPlan, keep the last 50 toggles as {idx, piece, prevBit} and add a 'Rückgängig' button next to the laying-mode toggle. Optionally add a row-by-row mode: tap a cell to mark the rest of that row within the selected section.
corrected:
1) Viewer.tsx onUp: when e.pointerType is 'touch' or 'pen', first find the target cell and piece as the code does now. Then compute its on-screen size: min(layout.colW[col], layout.rowH[row]) * view.scale for a full cell, or the bbox of the target piece's polygon for split or cut cells. If that size is under about 24 CSS px, do not call onPick. Instead animate a zoom (about 200 ms) centred on the tap point, up to the scale where that cell is about 40 px, capped at maxS. Show a short hint, 'Zum Verlegen/Auswählen hineinzoomen'. If the tap lands on a section label rectangle, select that section instead of toggling the hidden stone underneath.
2) Touch slop: raise it to 10 px for touch (keep 5 px for mouse). Treat a press longer than 500 ms as 'not a tap' (do not call onPick). Do not treat pointercancel as a tap: register a separate handler that only clears state.
3) StepPlan.tsx: keep an undo stack in state, capped at 50 entries. A single toggle pushes {idx, piece}; undo XORs the same bit again (togglePiecePlaced is an XOR, edits.ts:127). The section 'complete' and 'reset' actions push a copy of data.progress for that section's row/col range, restored with a small edits.ts helper. Show a 'Rückgängig (n)' button next to the 'Verlegemodus' toggle, plus a status line naming the last change, e.g. 'AP034 als verlegt markiert' / 'AP034 wieder offen' (use pieceId from layout.ts:184). This feedback stays readable at any zoom level.
4) After each toggle, set a transient highlight on that stone for about 600 ms by reusing the existing `highlight` prop. Drop navigator.vibrate, or add android.permission.VIBRATE to the manifest or use @capacitor/haptics, because without the permission it does nothing in the APK.
5) Optional: a row mode. In lay mode, a 'Reihe' segmented option marks every stone from the tapped cell to the end of that row within the selected section, pushing a single undo entry.
Tests: add an e2e touch test. Taps at fit zoom must not change placed-count; tap, zoom and tap must change it by 1; undo must return it to 0.

1. Viewer.tsx, onDown, onMove and onUp: store e.pointerType at pointer-down.
   - For touch and pen, use a tap slop of 10 px; keep 5 px for the mouse.
   - Before calling onPick, find the stone that was hit, as today (cellPieces and pointInPolygon). Compute its on-screen size as min(bbox(piece.poly).w, bbox(piece.poly).h) * view.scale.
   - For touch or pen, if that size is below 28 CSS px, do not call onPick. Call the existing zoomAt(p.x, p.y, k) with k chosen so that this stone becomes about 40 px (zoomAt already respects maxS = 120). Show a short hint, "Zum Antippen hineingezoomt" / "Zoomed in so you can tap a single stone" / tr equivalent.
   - A press longer than 500 ms never toggles. In laying mode, pass a new prop onLongPick(row, col, piece) so that a long press opens StoneDialog. That gives access to stone details without leaving laying mode. Outside laying mode, a long press is ignored.
   - Mouse behaviour stays as it is.
   - Apply the same logic in StepPreview, because it uses the same Viewer.

2. StepPlan.tsx, feedback after each toggle:
   - Set a transient flash state for 400 ms and pass it through the existing highlight prop.
   - Show a small toast with the real stone ID from the existing ID function, e.g. "AP034 verlegt" or "AP034 wieder offen", with a "Rückgängig" button.
   - Call navigator.vibrate?.(10), and add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.VIBRATE"/> to android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. Without it the WebView ignores the call. It is a normal permission, so the user sees no prompt.

3. Undo, kept in memory and limited to the last 50 steps.
   - Store entries as either {kind:'piece', idx, piece} (undo by toggling again) or {kind:'range', r0, r1, c0, c1, before: Uint16Array}. A range entry is a copy of data.progress for the section, taken before "Abschnitt fertig" or "Zurücksetzen".
   - Add a "Rückgängig (n)" button next to the laying-mode toggle and in the toast.
   - Undo restores the bits, checks piece < cellPieceCount(data, idx) before toggling, and calls api.touchProgress() so the saved data and the counts update.
   - Clear the stack whenever api.version changes (stone edits) or c.layout changes (recompute), because those reset progress and change the number of stones per cell.
   - Optionally add a confirmation to "Abschnitt fertig" when the section is partly laid. With undo in place this is not strictly needed.

4. Honesty (requirement 18): change the README.md undo row to "Rückgängig: nur für Verlegefortschritt (letzte 50 Schritte, nicht über Neuladen hinweg); Farb-/Formänderungen ohne Undo". Add the de, en and tr strings.

5. Tests, in e2e/run-e2e.cjs or a new touch spec with isMobile and hasTouch:
   - A tap at fit zoom in laying mode leaves placed-count unchanged and increases the zoom.
   - After that zoom, a tap lays exactly the stone under the finger, and a second tap 4 px away still hits the same stone.
   - A 1 s long press does not change the count.
   - "Abschnitt fertig" followed by "Rückgängig" restores the earlier count exactly, including partly laid sections.

Leave the row-by-row mode for a separate follow-up, such as "Bereich aufziehen = verlegt" using setRangePlaced, which already counts exactly.

findings.title: No undo/redo and no area or batch editing: every correction is one irreversible single-stone click
findings.problem: Requirement 13 (manually change stones, e.g. 'lighter blue') can only be done one piece at a time, and nothing can be undone. Removing a palette colour remaps every stone permanently. A shape change clears that cell's laying progress. A core function to replace a colour within a range already exists but is not reachable from the UI. Correcting a sky or a background means hundreds of separate clicks with no safety net.
findings.evidence: Reproduction /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/b1.cjs. Output: 'color before: 03 | after change: 04 | after ctrl+z: 04'. Grep finds no undo in src except 'free.undoPoint' (the freeform point editor). replaceColor in src/core/edits.ts:209 has no caller in src/ui. removePaletteColor is called from src/ui/project/StepColors.tsx:112. setCellKind sets progress to 0 (src/core/edits.ts:77). The README table lists 'Rückgängig (Undo): nicht vorhanden'.
findings.proposal: Add an EditJournal in src/core/edits.ts. Each operation stores CellSnapshot{idx, kind, c1, c2, sub?, line?, free?, progress} before and after; only the few affected Map entries are cloned. Palette operations store the previous palette plus the (idx, piece, oldColor) tuples they changed. Cap the stack at about 200 operations or 32 MB. Add ↶/↷ buttons in Preview and Plan, Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, and 'letzten Tap zurück' in laying mode. Add a selection tool in Viewer: a rectangle or lasso in mm, selecting by piece-centroid test. Actions on the selection or section: 'Farbe A → B' (reuse replaceColor with Range); 'heller/dunkler', which picks the palette colour with the smallest ΔE among those with L* ≥ current+3 or ≤ current−3; and 'Form zurücksetzen'. Each batch is one journal entry. Stats are recomputed by the existing worker path.

This bounds the worker queue and the cloned-mosaic memory to one copy, and stops real edits from waiting behind obsolete jobs. Measured today without this: 18.7 s latency after 12 taps on 3.1M.

3) Progress counters in a new pure module, src/core/progressIndex.ts:
- buildProgressIndex(layout, data, sections) makes one pass over all cells. It returns {secOfRow: Int32Array, secOfCol: Int32Array, placed: Int32Array(S), total: Int32Array(S)} and uses cellPieceCount as the only piece-count function.
- In useProject, rebuild it with useMemo keyed on [computed, sections, version]. Any compute, load, kind change, free-piece change or color edit therefore rebuilds it from data. It is never patched for those changes.
- Route every progress-only mutation through one function, applyProgressChange(index, data, idx, before, after). It adds popcount(after & m) - popcount(before & m) to placed[sec], where m = (1 << cellPieceCount) - 1. This covers togglePiecePlaced (StepPlan.tsx:100, StoneDialog.tsx:161) and setCellPlaced without assuming which direction the change goes.
- For setRangePlaced (StepPlan.tsx:210, 220), recount only that section.
- The progress useMemo (useProject.ts:222-228) reads placed[] and total[], with overall totals = sum over sections.
- total[] never changes on progress-only operations.

4) Tests in tests/progressIndex.test.ts, plus a dev-only assert:
- Run random sequences of toggle, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced, setCellKind, setFreePieces and setPieceColor, rebuilding the index on every version change.
- After each step, assert per-section placed and total equal progressOf(range).
- Assert the sum of total[] equals computeStats().pieces.
- Assert the selected-section per-color placed sum equals progressOf(section).placed.
- Align the edge cases (pieceCountFast default branch; cellPieces for LINE without params) so all three counts agree.

5) Scope honestly. This removes about 50-90 ms of main-thread work per tap at 1.4M-3.1M positions and removes the worker backlog. It does NOT fix tap latency at typical sizes on phones. At about 60k positions with 4x CPU, progressOf is about 4 ms of about 100 ms per tap, and the rest is the redraw and render pipeline. Track that as a separate, separately profiled finding.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
